memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Joseph brought his father Jacob in and presented him before Pharaoh. After Jacob blessed Pharaoh," — Gen 47:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Read that again slowly. An old shepherd, a refugee from a famine, with no land, no wealth and no political standing, stands before the most powerful ruler on earth — and blesses him.

Not the other way around.

By every worldly measure, Pharaoh is the greater man. He holds Jacob's survival in his hands. But Jacob carries something Pharaoh does not: he is a man of the covenant, an heir of the promise God made to Abraham that through his family all nations would be blessed (Gen 12:3). And so the old man blesses the king, because that is what he has to give.

Hebrews notes the principle plainly: the lesser person is blessed by the greater (Heb 7:7). In the room that day, spiritually speaking, Jacob was the greater man.

Do not measure your significance by what the world can see. You may have very little of what people count. But if you belong to Christ, you carry something the wealthiest person without Him does not have, and you have something to give in every room you enter.

Peter said it well to a beggar: silver or gold I do not have, but what I have I give you (Acts 3:6).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you measure your worth by what the world can see?
2. What do you actually have to give that money cannot buy?
3. Who could you bless this week, regardless of your own circumstances?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that in Christ I carry something more valuable than anything the world measures. Give me eyes to see it and courage to give it away. Amen.
